title: Distraught woman died in Oshawa holding cell
article: Christine Budgell was picked up by Durham police several times in the days leading up to her death in a downtown Oshawa station cell block, a coroner's jury heard Monday.

Jurors will hear from police officers, shelter workers and others who had contact with the troubled woman in the days before her death at 17 Division in January 2004, coroner's counsel Michael Blain said as the inquest began Monday in Whitby.

Ms. Budgell was picked up for public intoxication and lodged in the cells Jan. 17, 2004, Mr. Blain said. Officers found her hanging from a ligature made of socks attached to a ventilation grate; she was taken to hospital and died three days later.
"In the weeks preceding her death Christine Budgell faced a number of challenges," Mr. Blain said.

Fleeing an abusive relationship, Ms. Budgell was living in shelters and experiencing difficulties with alcohol, he said. On two occasions in the days leading up to Jan. 17 she had been taken into custody for public intoxication and held at the 17 Divisions cells until she was deemed sober, he said.
Ms. Budgell, 43, was distraught and very vocal when she was placed in custody Jan. 17, Mr. Blain said.
"She said she didn't want to be there; she wanted to go home," Mr. Blain said.
An officer had attempted to find out where Ms. Budgell was staying to take her there, but could not determine which shelter she was living at, Mr. Blain said.
On Monday, the five jurors were to hear expert witness evidence from a toxicologist and the pathologist who conducted an autopsy.
The inquest is presided over by Coroner William Lucas.
